what: Floating objects window — inside the panel, 50 copies of the same base shapes (cone, ball, arc, bottle, disc, egg, billiard ball, bowl) are drawn as three.js instances, each spinning on a random axis by .01rad per frame, while the whole panel turns on the y axis by .01. In screen space they drift along sine curves (time × .6) with a width of .5~7 horizontally, .5~7 vertically and 0~7 in depth, leaving the panel and coming back in. Each is .2~1× in size, lit by one light from the upper right plus a rim light. Pauses when the panel is off screen

options.shape: cone | sphere (default) | arc | bottle | disc | egg | ball | bowl
options.speed: Speed multiplier for rotating and drifting, default 1 (0 stops)

note: The original used 3D models (glb) such as a banana, sushi and a bottle. Parts are replaced with basic shapes of the same size and silhouette ratio, and the original shader is replaced by a fresh one with the same values (random rotation axis · float range .5~7 · time × .6). three r132 or later (library/_vendor/three@0.132.2/three.min.js)

from.where: index.js inner scene of the eight color windows — original InstancedMesh 50 · rotation3d(random.xyz, uTime) · sin float mix(.5,7) · uTime += .01/Frame
